root.label: Iterator invalidation
root.note: An iterator dies when storage or navigation structure changes; derive the rules from the layout.

children.label: Three questions
children.note: Ask: did elements move, did one die, did the structure used to find elements change.

children.label: Singular state
children.note: An invalidated iterator may only be assigned to or destroyed; any other use is undefined.

children.label: Iterators vs references
children.note: Iterators also depend on index structures, so they can die while references survive.

children.label: vector
children.note: Contiguous storage: reallocation moves everything, shifting moves the tail.

children.label: Reallocation
children.note: When size would exceed capacity, all iterators, pointers, references and end() are invalidated.

children.label: No reallocation
children.note: Insert or erase invalidates iterators and references at or after the change, plus end().

children.label: reserve guarantee
children.note: After reserve(n), appends up to capacity do not reallocate, so earlier iterators survive.

children.label: deque
children.note: Blocks plus an index: asymmetric rules for iterators and references.

children.label: End insertion
children.note: Push at either end invalidates all iterators including end(), but no references or pointers.

children.label: Erase at an end
children.note: Erasing the first (not last) element hits only that element; erasing the last also kills end().

children.label: Middle edit
children.note: Any insertion or erasure in the middle invalidates all iterators and references.

children.label: Node containers
children.note: list, forward_list, set, map and multi versions never move elements.

children.label: Insert
children.note: Insertion invalidates nothing.

children.label: Erase
children.note: Only iterators and references to the erased elements are invalidated; end() survives.

children.label: splice
children.note: Iterators remain valid but now belong to the destination list.

children.label: Unordered containers
children.note: Stable nodes, rebuildable bucket array.

children.label: Rehash
children.note: A rehash invalidates all iterators but not pointers or references to elements.

children.label: No rehash
children.note: Insertion without rehash invalidates nothing; erase affects only erased elements.

children.label: Special cases
children.note: Swap, move, string and end() need separate care.

children.label: swap and move
children.note: Iterators stay valid and refer into the other container; array swap exchanges values instead.

children.label: string
children.note: Conservative: almost any non-const member may invalidate; operator[], at, data and iterator getters do not.

children.label: Erase loops
children.note: Use it = c.erase(it) or std::erase_if; never reuse the erased iterator.
